title: D batch verify leftovers
description:
- [JMAP-wf92.10] minor crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs: Doc drift in the infallible expect() messages: they are swapped. Line 54 (calendar_get `ids: Option<&[Id]>`, still a slice) now says "Id Vec Serialize is infallible". Line 198 (`destroy`, now Option<Vec<Id>>) still says "Id slice Serialize is infallible". event.rs:58/201 and participant_identity.rs:41/160 have the same swap. This is only the text of panic messages on paths that cannot panic, so behaviour is unchanged.
- [JMAP-wf92.20] minor crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs: Outside the bead's literal scope (mail plus extension servers) and not tracked anywhere: the core jmap-server crate still has the dual-path pattern this bead removes elsewhere. `pub mod handlers;` (line 36) is public, yet `pub use handlers::{handle_changes, handle_get, handle_query, handle_query_changes, server_fail_from_backend, server_fail_value_from_backend, SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC}` (line 45) re-exports all 7 of its pub items at the root, so `jmap_server::handlers::handle_get` and `jmap_server::handle_get` name the same item. `pub mod backend` has the same pairing. JMAP-26di.47 covers only jmap-chat-client. The many types/client crates whose non-capability modules are `pub mod` and also root re-exported are likewise out of this bead's scope. Suggest a follow-up bead rather than a fix here.
- [JMAP-wf92.21] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs: MemoryBackend does not override the new privacy_conflicts hook, so it fails open on §5.9. The module docs call it a 'complete' reference implementation and it stores events, and the new backend.rs doc says 'backends that store events override it'. The working §5.9 logic exists only in the cfg(test) MockBackend (lib.rs test_support), so the integration tests in tests/*.rs, which run against MemoryBackend, never exercise the rule. Fail-open on may_copy_calendar_event is defensible because MemoryBackend has no account-ownership model. The bead only asked for hooks with fail-open defaults, so this is minor; it could go in a follow-up bead or be listed as a documented simplification.
- [JMAP-wf92.21] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs: The privacy_conflicts contract asks the backend to predict the account after the whole request, but it is called before any create, update or destroy is applied, and items can still fail afterwards (permission, notFound, the backend's own validation). The docs do not say that the backend must account for those failures. Concrete case: e1, e2 and e3 share a uid and are all public. The request updates e1 and e2 to private and destroys e3. The hook predicts a consistent post-state and approves both updates. If the destroy of e3 then fails with forbidden, the account ends with private and public events under one uid, which breaks the §5.9 MUST ('MUST have the same value'). The handler cannot fix this, so the hook's docs should spell out the obligation (or the handler should say the guarantee only holds for items that succeed).
- [JMAP-wf92.21] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs: No regression test covers the CHANGELOG 'Fixed' entry: a non-string element in destroy now gives invalidArguments before any create or update is applied. A test would send a valid create plus destroy [1] and assert both the method error and that nothing was created. There are also no tests for the error paths: privacy_conflicts returning Err should give a method-level serverFail with nothing applied, and may_copy_calendar_event returning Err should put serverFail in notCreated.
- [JMAP-wf92.21] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/README.md: Doc drift. The README covers CalendarEvent/set and /copy section by section (per-user routing, the utcStart/start §5.9 conflict, the copy flow) but does not mention the new uid/privacy check (invalidProperties ['privacy'] via privacy_conflicts) or the §5.10 forbidden check on copy (may_copy_calendar_event).
- [JMAP-510h.38] minor CHANGELOG.md: Entry (and the commit's `!` marker) labels #[non_exhaustive] on MemoryBackend as BREAKING, but every MemoryBackend already has only private fields, so code outside the crate could never build it with a struct literal or match it without `..`. The attribute changes nothing that code can observe, and the commit body itself says it only states intent. The label only matters if it pushes a version bump that isn't needed (low impact in 0.x next to real breaking entries).
